verdict.rationale: mise documents a single checked-in config. It supports platform-keyed tool entries (e.g. macos-x64) and bootstrap features covering macOS defaults and Linux accounts, which points to one config spanning macOS and Linux. However, Windows is never mentioned, and some features are explicitly limited to Linux and macOS (sandboxing) or to Linux only (accounts). missing for 10: any evidence of Windows support, explicit documentation that the same workflow and config behave identically across all three OSes, independent cross-platform hands-on reports.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use the same workflow and config on macOS, Linux, and Windows

citations.quote: mise bootstrap sets up a new computer from the same file: OS packages, git repos, dotfiles, shell activation, macOS defaults, and services, then your tools.
Creates, updates, or removes the local accounts declared in `[bootstrap.users]` and `[bootstrap.groups]` on Linux.
Sandboxing | Off; Linux and macOS only
Use tasks for builds, tests, linters, development servers, and other commands you want teammates and CI to run consistently.
